- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.20) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent prices are falling.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak or use moving average to smooth.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day forecasts when sentiment is flat (0.00); add 2–5% buffer if no strong sentiment signal.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days above 75) and model is rising, reduce forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, if model is rising steadily but true outcome shows volatility or divergence, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day of lagged divergence.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and model is rising, check for lagged price reversal; if true outcome drops after 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 2–4% per day.
